findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator crashes on datetime keys used by audit logs
findings.body: The new OptimizedCursorPaginator implements get_item_key by calling math.floor/math.ceil on the raw model attribute. The audit-log endpoint selects this paginator with order_by="-datetime", so the attribute is a datetime and the first page raises TypeError. Its value_from_cursor also returns the raw integer cursor value instead of converting it back to a datetime, so even if the key conversion were fixed, build_queryset would compare a datetime column against an integer. Any request with optimized_pagination=true for a superuser or globally privileged member returns a 500.

findings.title: Negative-offset branch slices Django QuerySet with a negative index
findings.body: When enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset is negative, get_result assigns start_offset=cursor.offset and evaluates queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing and raise ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported"); the stop value is also computed from the negative start and may be negative or nonsensical. Cursor.from_string accepts negative offsets, so a crafted cursor can trigger this path instead of the intended advanced pagination behavior.

findings.title: Changing span-buf:s keys from sets to sorted sets breaks rolling deployment
findings.body: The buffer now writes span payloads with zadd and reads/merges them with zcard/zscan/zunionstore, but the Redis key namespace span-buf:s is unchanged while old deployments stored those keys as Redis sets. During a rolling deploy, old and new consumers will operate on the same keys with conflicting types: zadd/zcard/zscan on an existing set and sadd on an existing zset both raise WRONGTYPE. Unflushed segments created before the deploy will therefore fail ingestion/flushing until their TTL expires unless the keys are migrated or the namespace is versioned.

findings.title: Span-count limit is no longer enforced when loading segments
findings.body: The max_segment_spans check was removed from _load_segment_data, and SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans is now unused; eviction is instead hard-coded to 1000 inside the Lua script. If the Python zadd pipeline writes more than 1000 spans and the following EVALSHA calls fail or the process dies between the two pipelines, the set is never evicted. Because the loader no longer rejects oversized segments, such a set can be flushed downstream. The constructor option also no longer controls anything, and its default of 1001 no longer matches the hard-coded 1000 cap.

findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE default aggregation corrupts eviction scores for duplicate spans
findings.body: The two zunionstore calls use the default SUM aggregation. If the same span payload exists in both the destination set and the set being merged (for example, at-least-once duplicate delivery after a parent merge), its score becomes the sum of the two end_timestamp_precise values rather than the actual timestamp. Subsequent zpopmin eviction then treats that duplicate as newer than it really is and may evict newer spans instead. Using AGGREGATE MAX (or MIN, depending on the desired tie behavior) would preserve timestamp semantics.

findings.title: Redirect-chain limit reduced from 10000 to 1000 without handling deep traces
findings.body: The parent-redirect walk now stops after 1000 iterations, down from 10000. For segment trees deeper than that, set_span_id will remain an intermediate span instead of resolving to the root, so later spans can be placed in the wrong segment. The change is intentional-looking but untested; if the lower bound is desired it should be justified and covered, otherwise it is a silent regression for very deep traces.

findings.title: No test covers the new eviction cap or duplicate-score behavior
findings.body: The PR's central behavior is eviction during insert, but every buffer test inserts at most five spans. There is no test that pushes a segment past 1000 spans and asserts that the oldest entries are evicted, no test that verifies max_segment_spans is still honored or intentionally removed, and no test for the zunionstore duplicate-member score behavior. A regression in the cap or in the removed load-time guard would pass CI.
